title: Advisor and report backgrounds (tiles.dll 50-59, 65, 66)
author: Richard Penman
license: MIT, as the rest of this repository (LICENSE)
method: AI-generated: Google Gemini 3 Pro Image (model id gemini-3-pro-image) via the Gemini API generateContent endpoint, responseModalities IMAGE, aspectRatio 3:2, imageSize 2K (2528x1696 JPEG), one prompt plus two reference images per request; then prepared deterministically with Pillow
originalGameArtwork: No original-game image was supplied to the model or used as a pixel source. Screenshots of the original reports were used only to measure the contrast of the game's text colours.
promptTemplate: A painted background for a strategy game's {report}, in the same painterly digital-illustration style as the first two reference images. Subject: {subject} Treatment: very dark and muted, almost monochrome charcoal and slate grey with a slight {tint} tint; low contrast; soft, even lighting with no bright highlights; overall brightness about 35% (average colour near RGB 90, 90, 90). Composition: the left two thirds and the top quarter must be calm, empty, low-detail areas, because rows of white and yellow text and small icons are drawn over them; keep the busier details near the right and bottom edges. No text, letters, numbers, labels, logos, frames, borders or vignette; {nowriting} Landscape, 3:2. Match the brushwork and palette of the reference images.
preparation: The generated image is scaled (Lanczos) to cover the area the window shows of the 640x480 picture at density 2 (the advisors' top-left 600x400 logical pixels: 1200x800; the tax-rate dialog's 400x256 on small screens: 800x512, and 600x384 on large ones, prepared as the advisors'), cropped about its centre and placed top-left on a 1280x960 canvas; the remaining right margin is the area mirrored about its right edge and the remaining bottom margin the resulting rows mirrored about their bottom edge. The masters here reproduce pixel-for-pixel from the generated outputs with that step (Pillow 13.0.0). 65 and 66 are one painting.
selection: Each background was chosen for the legibility of the game's text drawn over it: at least 4.5:1 WCAG contrast for every text colour of its window except the civilizations' blue (0,115,255), which cannot reach 4.5:1 on any ground lighter than near-black (2.9 to 3.4:1 on these against 1.6 to 1.9:1 on the original game art), and by eye; a new painting was requested where a candidate fell short (56 and 57 are the third).
